question: An incident report in a hospital is written mainly to:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. record the facts of an untoward event for review and prevention

🧠 Clinical Rationale: An incident report is a factual record of an untoward event, kept so that the cause is studied and the same thing is prevented from happening again

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — replace the nurse's notes in the case sheet: The nurse's notes in the case sheet remain the clinical record and the incident report is an additional administrative document

C — punish the staff member who was at fault: Disciplinary action, if any, is a separate matter decided after enquiry

D — inform the patient's relatives of the mistake: The relatives are informed by the doctor and not through an incident report

⚠️ Exam Trap: Remember that delegation transfers the task but never the accountability.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse writes the incident report on the facts alone and never on opinion, because an incident report written in anger is the document most likely to be read out in a court
option_1: replace the nurse's notes in the case sheet
option_2: record the facts of an untoward event for review and prevention
option_3: punish the staff member who was at fault
option_4: inform the patient's relatives of the mistake

question: At the change of shift a staff nurse finds that a 62 year old diabetic patient was given 10 units of insulin instead of 4 units two hours ago and the patient is now sweating and drowsy. The nurse should FIRST:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. treat the hypoglycaemia, inform the doctor and then report the incident

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The patient comes first, so the low sugar is treated at once, the doctor is informed and the incident report follows while the facts are fresh

🔍 Key Clues: 62 year old

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — hand the matter over to the next shift and go home: A matter handed over to the next shift loses the details and delays the treatment

C — enter the event only in the nurse's personal diary: A personal diary has no legal standing and is never a substitute for the official record

D — complete the incident report before doing anything else: Paperwork before the patient leaves the hypoglycaemia untreated

⚠️ Exam Trap: Remember that delegation transfers the task but never the accountability.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse treats first and documents immediately afterwards, because a report written within the hour is accurate and one written at the end of the shift is a reconstruction
option_1: hand the matter over to the next shift and go home
option_2: treat the hypoglycaemia, inform the doctor and then report the incident
option_3: enter the event only in the nurse's personal diary
option_4: complete the incident report before doing anything else

question: In patient safety language a near miss means:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. an error that was intercepted before it could reach the patient

🧠 Clinical Rationale: A near miss is an error or a dangerous situation that was caught in time and so never reached the patient

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — an error that reached the patient and caused harm: An error that reaches the patient and harms him is an adverse event

B — a death that was expected in the course of the illness: An expected death is not an error at all

D — an error that was discovered after the patient was discharged: An error found after discharge is a late detected adverse event

⚠️ Exam Trap: Remember that delegation transfers the task but never the accountability.

💎 PNC Pearl: Near misses are reported as freely as the actual errors, because the near miss tells the ward where its system is weak while no harm has yet been done
option_1: an error that reached the patient and caused harm
option_2: a death that was expected in the course of the illness
option_3: an error that was intercepted before it could reach the patient
option_4: an error that was discovered after the patient was discharged

question: In a mass casualty incident 40 injured patients arrive within twenty minutes and the nursing officer has only six nurses. The most appropriate action is to:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. post one nurse with each of the six most seriously injured patients and ask for additional staff at once

🧠 Clinical Rationale: In a crisis the nursing resource is concentrated where it saves life, and additional staff are requested without delay

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — give routine care to all the patients strictly in the order of arrival: First come first served wastes the nurses on the minor injuries while the seriously injured wait

C — wait until the doctors have examined every patient before starting any nursing care: Nursing care and medical examination run together in an emergency and never one after the other

D — send all the walking injured home without examination: The walking injured still need triage, first aid and observation

⚠️ Exam Trap: Remember that delegation transfers the task but never the accountability.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nursing officer in a disaster identifies the six patients whose next hour decides their survival and puts a named nurse with each of them, because staff spread thinly over forty patients save none
option_1: post one nurse with each of the six most seriously injured patients and ask for additional staff at once
option_2: give routine care to all the patients strictly in the order of arrival
option_3: wait until the doctors have examined every patient before starting any nursing care
option_4: send all the walking injured home without examination

question: The five rights of delegation include all of the following EXCEPT:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. right salary

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The five rights are the right task, the right person, the right direction and communication, the right supervision and the right circumstances, and pay has no place among them

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — right task: The right task is the first of the five rights

C — right supervision: The right supervision and evaluation is the last of the five rights

D — right person: The right person means matching the work to the competence of the worker

⚠️ Exam Trap: Remember that delegation transfers the task but never the accountability.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse who delegates remembers that the accountability is never delegated with the task, because the registered nurse remains answerable for the care that was given

question: A 48 year old patient with a clean sutured abdominal wound needs a dressing change and the ward is very busy. The registered nurse should:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. delegate to the nursing assistant after checking the wound, the assistant's competence and her own availability to supervise

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Delegation is safe when the task is suitable, the worker is competent and the delegator remains available to supervise and to be answerable

🔍 Key Clues: 48 year old

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — delegate and leave the ward for a tea break: A nurse who delegates and walks away has neither supervised nor remained answerable

B — ask the patient's relative to do the dressing: A relative is not a trained worker and cannot be given nursing care to perform

D — refuse to delegate, because every dressing is the duty of a registered nurse: A simple clean dressing may be delegated where the policy of the hospital allows it

⚠️ Exam Trap: Remember that delegation transfers the task but never the accountability.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse who delegates says clearly what is to be done, when to stop and whom to call, because an assistant left with an unclear instruction is the commonest source of a delayed complication
option_1: delegate and leave the ward for a tea break
option_2: ask the patient's relative to do the dressing
option_3: delegate to the nursing assistant after checking the wound, the assistant's competence and her own availability to supervise
option_4: refuse to delegate, because every dressing is the duty of a registered nurse

question: The legal strength of a nurse's record depends chiefly on the fact that it is:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. a contemporaneous, factual and signed record

🧠 Clinical Rationale: A record made at the time of the event, stating facts and signed by the nurse, is the record that carries weight

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — kept only in the ward register: The official case record is the legal document and not a private ward register

C — written in the nurse's own words with her opinions: Opinions and conclusions have no place in a clinical record and weaken it

D — written at the end of the shift from memory: A record reconstructed from memory at the end of the shift is easily questioned

⚠️ Exam Trap: Remember that delegation transfers the task but never the accountability.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse writes what she saw and did, not what she thought, because the sentence written at the bedside is the one that protects the patient and the nurse both
option_3: written in the nurse's own words with her opinions
option_4: written at the end of the shift from memory

question: An 82 year old patient with left hemiplegia is found on the floor beside the bed at 2 am. The nurse's note should contain:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. the time, the position in which he was found, the injuries, the vital signs, the doctor informed and the action taken

🧠 Clinical Rationale: A fall note is complete when it records the time, the findings, the injuries, the observations made and the people informed

🔍 Key Clues: 82 year old

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — a short note written after the morning round: A note written hours later raises the question of what was done in the meantime

C — only the words "patient fell down": A bare statement gives no idea of the patient's condition and no evidence of the care given

D — the nurse's opinion that the patient was careless: Blaming the patient is an opinion and has no place in the record

⚠️ Exam Trap: Remember that delegation transfers the task but never the accountability.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse records the neuro observations and the limb movements after every fall, because a delay of hours between a fall and the discovery of a bleeding inside the head is what makes such cases indefensible
option_1: a short note written after the morning round
option_2: the time, the position in which he was found, the injuries, the vital signs, the doctor informed and the action taken
option_4: the nurse's opinion that the patient was careless

question: A nursing quality indicator is best described as:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. a measure of the structure, process or outcome of care followed over time

🧠 Clinical Rationale: A quality indicator is a measurable element of care that is tracked over time or against a standard so that the care can be judged and improved

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — the number of complaints received in a year: Complaints are one source of data and not an indicator in themselves

C — the number of beds sanctioned for a hospital: The bed strength of a hospital says nothing about the quality of the care given in it

D — the total number of nurses on duty in a ward: Staff numbers are an input and become an indicator only when related to a standard of care

⚠️ Exam Trap: Remember that delegation transfers the task but never the accountability.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse records the indicator the same way every time, because an indicator measured differently by each shift can be made to show any trend the ward wishes
option_1: a measure of the structure, process or outcome of care followed over time
option_2: the number of complaints received in a year
option_3: the number of beds sanctioned for a hospital
option_4: the total number of nurses on duty in a ward

question: A hospital audit shows that the surgical site infection rate has risen from 2 per cent to 6 per cent in three months. The nursing officer should:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. review the sterilisation, hand hygiene and dressing practices against the standard and correct the gaps found

🧠 Clinical Rationale: A rising rate is a signal to study the process against the standard, find the weak step and correct it

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — wait for the next quarter to see whether the rate falls by itself: An infection rate that has tripled in three months will not correct itself and the patients keep paying meanwhile

C — blame the theatre staff at the next meeting: Blame finds no cause and drives the reporting underground

D — keep the figures out of the committee report: Suppressing the figures removes the chance of improvement and is unethical

⚠️ Exam Trap: Remember that delegation transfers the task but never the accountability.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nursing officer brings the figures to the staff with the process attached, because a staff that sees where the break in the chain occurred mends it and a staff that is blamed hides the next one
option_1: wait for the next quarter to see whether the rate falls by itself
option_2: review the sterilisation, hand hygiene and dressing practices against the standard and correct the gaps found
option_3: blame the theatre staff at the next meeting
option_4: keep the figures out of the committee report

question: During a busy shift two staff nurses quarrel loudly about the duty roster in front of the patients. The nursing officer should:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. hear both of them, keep the patient care running and settle the matter privately after the shift

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The immediate need is to keep the work moving and the patients undisturbed, and the dispute is then resolved in private with both sides heard

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — support the senior nurse at once in front of everyone: Taking sides in public hardens the quarrel and damages the confidence of the other nurse

B — ignore the quarrel because it is a personal matter: A quarrel inside a ward is not personal because it disturbs the care and the patients

C — change both their shifts immediately: Punishing both without enquiry settles nothing and leaves the cause in place

⚠️ Exam Trap: Remember that delegation transfers the task but never the accountability.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nursing officer separates the persons from the problem and asks what each needs to do the work, because most quarrels in a ward are about work and only appear to be about people
option_1: support the senior nurse at once in front of everyone
option_2: ignore the quarrel because it is a personal matter
option_4: hear both of them, keep the patient care running and settle the matter privately after the shift

question: A fire breaks out in a 30 bed ward of a hospital. The FIRST priority of the nurse in charge is to:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. raise the alarm, evacuate the patients who cannot move themselves and direct the staff by name

🧠 Clinical Rationale: In a fire the alarm, the evacuation of the helpless patients and clear directions to the staff by name take priority over everything else

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — save the costly equipment of the ward: Equipment is replaceable and patients are not

B — put out the fire herself with the nearest extinguisher: One nurse on the fire is one nurse less for the evacuation and the alarm has not yet been raised

D — complete the ward register before leaving: The register can be carried out at the end and never delays the evacuation

⚠️ Exam Trap: Remember that delegation transfers the task but never the accountability.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse in charge assigns the evacuation by name and by bed, because in a fire the staff who wait for a general instruction lose the two minutes that would have got the last patient out
option_1: save the costly equipment of the ward
option_2: put out the fire herself with the nearest extinguisher
option_3: raise the alarm, evacuate the patients who cannot move themselves and direct the staff by name

question: A budget in a nursing department is best described as:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. a written plan of the expected income and expenditure for a stated period

🧠 Clinical Rationale: A budget is a financial plan made in advance for a definite period against which the actual spending is later compared

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — the number of patients treated in a year: The patient load influences the budget but is not the budget itself

C — the list of equipment already purchased: A purchase list records what has been bought and not what is planned

D — the total salary paid to the nurses in a month: Salaries are one item of expenditure within the budget

⚠️ Exam Trap: Remember that delegation transfers the task but never the accountability.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nursing officer prepares the budget from the actual ward consumption of the last year, because a budget built on guesswork fails at the first shortage of a consumable in the middle of a month
option_1: the number of patients treated in a year
option_2: a written plan of the expected income and expenditure for a stated period
option_4: the total salary paid to the nurses in a month

question: During a dengue outbreak the oxygen cylinders of a 200 bed hospital fall to a two day stock. The nursing officer should FIRST:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. count what is left, work out the daily consumption and place an urgent indent with the administration

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The action that buys time is an accurate count, a realistic estimate of the daily use and an urgent indent raised at once through the proper channel

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — borrow from a private supplier at any price without informing anyone: An emergency purchase made without authority cannot be repeated and breaks the financial rules of the hospital

B — restrict oxygen to the most serious patients without telling the doctors: Deciding alone who will get oxygen is a clinical decision that belongs to the treating team

C — place the routine monthly indent and wait its turn: The routine indent will arrive after the stock has finished

⚠️ Exam Trap: Remember that delegation transfers the task but never the accountability.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nursing officer keeps a running tally of the critical consumables each shift, because the shortage that is discovered on the day it happens is the one that cannot be covered
option_1: borrow from a private supplier at any price without informing anyone
option_2: restrict oxygen to the most serious patients without telling the doctors
option_3: place the routine monthly indent and wait its turn
option_4: count what is left, work out the daily consumption and place an urgent indent with the administration

question: Patient classification for the purpose of nursing staffing means grouping patients according to:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. the amount of nursing care each of them needs

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Patients are grouped by the hours and the complexity of nursing care they require, and the nurse to patient ratio is then fixed for each group

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — their age group: Age influences care needs but is not the basis of classification

C — the ward in which they are admitted: The ward is the place of care and not the measure of it

D — their medical diagnosis: Two patients with the same diagnosis may need very different amounts of nursing

⚠️ Exam Trap: Remember that delegation transfers the task but never the accountability.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nursing officer recalculates the category of each patient every shift, because a patient who was self caring yesterday and is dependent today is the one who is missed when the classification is left unchanged
option_1: the amount of nursing care each of them needs
option_3: the ward in which they are admitted

question: The measure of central tendency that is most affected by an extreme value is the:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. mean

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The mean uses every value in the series, so a single very high or very low value pulls it away from the centre

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — median: The median depends only on the middle position and is barely moved

C — range: The range is a measure of spread and is not a measure of central tendency at all

D — mode: The mode is the commonest value and an extreme reading does not change it

⚠️ Exam Trap: In research questions define the term precisely - reliability, validity and sampling are often interchanged.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse studying the length of stay reports the median as well as the mean, because one patient who stayed for four months can make the average stay of a whole ward look false

question: A nurse records the birth weights of 50 newborn babies in a labour room and wants to show how many babies fall in each weight band of 500 grams. The most suitable diagram is a:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. histogram

🧠 Clinical Rationale: A histogram is a series of adjacent bars on a continuous scale and is the diagram for grouped continuous data such as weight bands

🔍 Key Clues: newborn

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — line diagram: A line diagram is used to show a trend over time

C — pie diagram: A pie diagram shows the proportion of a whole and is not used for continuous grouping

D — pictogram: A pictogram shows rough quantities with small pictures and is used for simple comparison

⚠️ Exam Trap: In research questions define the term precisely - reliability, validity and sampling are often interchanged.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse draws the weight distribution before calculating anything, because the shape of the histogram tells at once whether the mean is a fair summary of the ward's babies

question: A bar diagram differs from a histogram mainly because in a bar diagram:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. the bars are separated by spaces and the data are not continuous

🧠 Clinical Rationale: In a bar diagram the bars are separate and are used for data that fall into distinct classes such as wards or years, while a histogram is used for continuous grouped data

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — the values are shown as angles: Values shown as angles belong to the pie diagram

B — the bars are always drawn touching each other: Adjacent bars without gaps belong to the histogram

C — the bars represent the same quantity in every case: The height of each bar varies with the value it represents

⚠️ Exam Trap: In research questions define the term precisely - reliability, validity and sampling are often interchanged.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse chooses a bar diagram when the classes are named and a histogram when the classes are measured, because mixing the two makes a correct figure look careless to the examiner
option_2: the bars are always drawn touching each other
option_3: the bars represent the same quantity in every case
option_4: the bars are separated by spaces and the data are not continuous

question: In a pie diagram of 200 patients, a category with 50 patients is shown by an angle of:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. 90 degrees

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Fifty out of two hundred is one quarter of the total, and one quarter of 360 degrees is 90 degrees

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — 45 degrees: 45 degrees would represent one eighth of the total, or 25 patients

B — 120 degrees: 120 degrees would represent one third of the total, or about 67 patients

C — 180 degrees: 180 degrees would represent half of the total, or 100 patients

⚠️ Exam Trap: In research questions define the term precisely - reliability, validity and sampling are often interchanged.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse checks that the angles of a pie diagram add up to 360 degrees, because a chart that does not close its circle shows that a category has been counted twice or left out

question: A frequency polygon is obtained by:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. joining the midpoints of the tops of the bars of a histogram

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The frequency polygon is drawn by joining the midpoints of the class intervals and is a line version of the histogram

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — joining the actual values of a series with straight lines: Joining raw values with straight lines gives a line diagram of a time series

C — drawing separate bars for each class: Separate bars describe the bar diagram

D — dividing the circle into sectors: Sectors of a circle describe the pie diagram

⚠️ Exam Trap: In research questions define the term precisely - reliability, validity and sampling are often interchanged.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse compares two distributions on one graph with two frequency polygons, because two sets of bars drawn one over the other hide whichever is shorter
option_1: joining the midpoints of the tops of the bars of a histogram
option_2: joining the actual values of a series with straight lines

question: The standard deviation of a set of observations measures:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. the average distance of the observations from the mean

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The standard deviation is the root mean square of the deviations of the readings from their own mean and expresses how widely they are scattered

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — the difference between the largest and the smallest observation: The gap between the largest and the smallest reading is the range

C — the commonest value of the observations: The commonest value is the mode

D — the middle value of the observations: The middle value is the median

⚠️ Exam Trap: In research questions define the term precisely - reliability, validity and sampling are often interchanged.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse reports the mean with its standard deviation, because a mean of 37.5 degrees that came from readings of 37.4 to 37.6 tells a very different story from the same mean that came from readings of 34 and 41
option_1: the difference between the largest and the smallest observation
option_2: the average distance of the observations from the mean

question: In a community of 20,000 people, 120 infants were born in a year and 6 infants died before completing one year of age. The infant mortality rate is:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. 50 per 1,000 live births

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The infant mortality rate is the deaths under one year divided by the live births in the same year, multiplied by a thousand, so six divided by one hundred and twenty gives 50

🔍 Key Clues: infant

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — 30 per 1,000 live births: Thirty per thousand would need a divisor of two hundred births

B — 3 per 1,000 live births: Three per thousand would need only 0.36 deaths

C — 6 per 1,000 live births: Six per thousand would be the number of deaths without division by the births

⚠️ Exam Trap: In research questions define the term precisely - reliability, validity and sampling are often interchanged.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse uses the number of live births as the denominator for infant deaths and the mid year population for deaths at all ages, because using the wrong denominator is the commonest statistical error in a community report

question: The daily pulse rates of one patient over nine days are 76, 78, 80, 82, 84, 86, 88 and 90. The median pulse rate is:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. 83

🧠 Clinical Rationale: With the eight readings placed in order the middle falls between the fourth and the fifth value, so the median is the average of 82 and 84

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — 86: 86 is not a middle value of this series

B — 84: 84 is the upper of the two middle readings only

C — 82: 82 is the lower of the two middle readings only

⚠️ Exam Trap: In research questions define the term precisely - reliability, validity and sampling are often interchanged.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse arranges the readings in order before taking a middle value, because the median of an unordered list is simply the middle line of that list and will usually be wrong

question: For grouped data the mode is taken as:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. the midpoint of the class with the highest frequency

🧠 Clinical Rationale: In grouped frequency data the modal class is the class with the greatest frequency and its midpoint is taken as the mode

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — the class with the lowest frequency: The class with the least frequency is the least typical value in the set

B — the average of the first and the last class marks: The average of the first and the last class mark has no statistical meaning

C — the difference between the highest and the lowest frequency: A difference of frequencies is a measure of spread and not a measure of central tendency

⚠️ Exam Trap: In research questions define the term precisely - reliability, validity and sampling are often interchanged.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse checks that the modal class is not merely a class made artificially wide, because a wide interval collects more patients by its size alone and can create a mode that does not exist
option_2: the average of the first and the last class marks
option_3: the difference between the highest and the lowest frequency
option_4: the midpoint of the class with the highest frequency

question: A line diagram is most useful for showing:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. the trend of an event over a period of time

🧠 Clinical Rationale: A line diagram plots a series against time and brings out the rise, the fall and the seasonal pattern at a glance

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — the proportion of each part in a whole: The proportion of the parts of a whole is shown by a pie diagram

B — the frequency of grouped continuous data: The frequency of grouped continuous data is shown by a histogram

C — the comparison of two unrelated quantities: Two unrelated quantities are best compared with a bar diagram

⚠️ Exam Trap: In research questions define the term precisely - reliability, validity and sampling are often interchanged.

💎 PNC Pearl: The community nurse plots the malaria cases month by month on a line diagram, because the peak month on the graph is the month for which the spraying and the camps must be planned
option_1: the proportion of each part in a whole
option_4: the trend of an event over a period of time

question: The monthly figures of dengue cases in a district from January to December are to be presented so that the seasonal rise is seen at once. The best choice is a:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. line diagram

🧠 Clinical Rationale: A line diagram keeps the months in their natural order and so displays the rise and the fall of the epidemic clearly

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — bar diagram with the months rearranged in order of size: Rearranging the months by size destroys the very pattern that is to be shown

C — pie diagram: A pie diagram loses the sequence of the months altogether

D — scatter diagram: A scatter diagram is used to show the relation between two variables and not a time trend

⚠️ Exam Trap: In research questions define the term precisely - reliability, validity and sampling are often interchanged.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse keeps the time axis in its true order and starts it at zero, because a time axis that is broken or rearranged can make a falling epidemic look like a rising one
option_1: bar diagram with the months rearranged in order of size

question: A researcher selects the first 50 patients attending a clinic on a Monday morning as the sample. This is an example of:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. purposive sampling

🧠 Clinical Rationale: When the sample is chosen deliberately for convenience or for a particular characteristic, the method is purposive or convenience sampling and cannot be generalised to the whole population

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — systematic sampling: Systematic sampling takes every nth member after a random start

C — simple random sampling: Simple random sampling gives every member of the population an equal chance of selection

D — stratified sampling: Stratified sampling divides the population into groups and draws from each group

⚠️ Exam Trap: In research questions define the term precisely - reliability, validity and sampling are often interchanged.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse reads how the sample was drawn before accepting a conclusion, because a convenient sample can describe the ward it came from and can never speak for the district

question: The difference between reliability and validity of an instrument is that reliability is about:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. the consistency of the measurements and validity is about measuring what is intended

🧠 Clinical Rationale: A reliable tool gives the same reading again and again and a valid tool measures the attribute it claims to measure

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — the language used and validity is about the scoring key: Language and scoring affect the usefulness of a tool but do not define the two terms

C — the cost of the instrument and validity is about its appearance: Cost and appearance have nothing to do with either property

D — the number of items and validity is about the length of the study: The number of items and the length of the study are unrelated to the two concepts

⚠️ Exam Trap: In research questions define the term precisely - reliability, validity and sampling are often interchanged.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse checks the validity before the reliability, because a weighing scale that reads the same wrong weight every time is perfectly reliable and quite useless for the patient
option_1: the consistency of the measurements and validity is about measuring what is intended
option_2: the language used and validity is about the scoring key
option_3: the cost of the instrument and validity is about its appearance
option_4: the number of items and validity is about the length of the study

question: To find out whether a new dressing reduces the rate of wound infection, patients are allotted to the two dressing methods by a toss of a coin and neither the patient nor the assessor knows which dressing was used. This design is a:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. double blind randomised controlled trial

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Random allotment with both the patient and the assessor kept unaware of the treatment is the double blind randomised controlled trial and gives the strongest evidence

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — descriptive survey: A descriptive survey only describes what is happening

B — retrospective record review: A record review is also retrospective and carries the errors of the original records

D — case control study: A case control study looks backwards from the outcome and cannot establish cause

⚠️ Exam Trap: In research questions define the term precisely - reliability, validity and sampling are often interchanged.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse notes who did the randomisation, because a trial in which the allotment could have been foreseen loses the very protection that randomisation was meant to give

⚠️ Exam Trap: In obstetric questions ask who is at immediate risk, mother or fetus - that decides the first action.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse teaches the danger signs with the words the woman uses herself, because a woman who is told to watch for oedema will not recognise the puffy face and the tight ring that she sees in her own mirror
option_2: swelling of the face and the hands

question: A mother brings a two month old infant to the sub centre for the first dose of the routine immunisation. The nurse should give:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. BCG, oral polio and the first dose of pentavalent

🧠 Clinical Rationale: At six weeks the infant is due for BCG, the oral polio drops and the first dose of the pentavalent vaccine, which may all be given in the same visit

🔍 Key Clues: infant

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — measles and vitamin A: Measles and vitamin A belong to the ninth month

C — the second dose of pentavalent: The second dose comes four weeks after the first

D — only BCG: BCG alone leaves the infant unprotected against diphtheria, pertussis, tetanus, hepatitis B and Haemophilus influenzae type b

⚠️ Exam Trap: In community health questions ask whether the action is at family, community or facility level.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse records the date and the site of each injection, because an immunisation record that cannot be read is the reason a child is either over vaccinated or left unprotected
option_1: BCG, oral polio and the first dose of pentavalent

question: An epidemic is best defined as:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. the occurrence of cases of a disease in a community in excess of what is normally expected

🧠 Clinical Rationale: An epidemic is the occurrence in a community of cases of an illness in numbers clearly above the expected level for that place and time

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — a disease that is present in a community all the time: A disease present all the time is endemic

C — the usual number of cases of a disease in a community over a period: The usual number of cases describes the endemic level

D — a disease that occurs in a single family: A single family is too small a unit to be called an epidemic

⚠️ Exam Trap: In community health questions ask whether the action is at family, community or facility level.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse reports the first few cases above the expected number and does not wait for the count to look large, because an epidemic that is reported late has already passed the point at which it could be contained
option_1: a disease that is present in a community all the time
option_2: the occurrence of cases of a disease in a community in excess of what is normally expected
option_3: the usual number of cases of a disease in a community over a period
option_4: a disease that occurs in a single family

question: The aim of the Directly Observed Treatment Short course in the tuberculosis programme is to:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. ensure that every dose of the antitubercular treatment is actually swallowed under observation

🧠 Clinical Rationale: A trained observer watches the patient swallow each dose, which prevents irregular intake and the rise of drug resistance

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — give free drugs to the patient for a year: The drugs are free, but that is a part of the programme and not its purpose

B — isolate the patient from the family: Isolation is not required, since pulmonary tuberculosis becomes non infectious after a few weeks of regular treatment

C — vaccinate the contacts of the patient: Contact vaccination is done for the children in the household and is separate from the treatment strategy

⚠️ Exam Trap: In community health questions ask whether the action is at family, community or facility level.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse records the dose taken and never hands over a week's stock in the place of observation, because irregular treatment is what turns a curable disease into multi drug resistant tuberculosis
option_1: give free drugs to the patient for a year
option_4: ensure that every dose of the antitubercular treatment is actually swallowed under observation

question: A newborn weighing 2.2 kg at birth in a cold labour room has a temperature of 35.8 degrees and is not feeding well. The nurse should FIRST:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. place him skin to skin on the mother's chest, cover both and recheck the temperature

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Skin to skin contact with the mother, a warm cap and a warm blanket raise the temperature of a mildly cold newborn quickly and safely, and the temperature is then rechecked

🔍 Key Clues: newborn | 2.2 kg

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — give him a bottle feed: A baby who is not feeding well and is cold must be warmed before feeding and should be breast fed

B — bathe the baby to clean him: Bathing a cold newborn lowers the temperature further

D — put him in a cot away from the mother: A cot away from the mother loses the cheapest and the best source of warmth

⚠️ Exam Trap: In paediatric questions look at the age first - the normal values and the expected action change with age.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse takes the axillary temperature of every newborn on arrival in the ward and after each feed, because a cold baby stops feeding, and a baby who stops feeding becomes colder still
option_3: place him skin to skin on the mother's chest, cover both and recheck the temperature
option_4: put him in a cot away from the mother

question: An 18 month old child who has not yet started to walk is brought to the clinic. The nurse should FIRST:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. take a full history of the milestones, the birth and the feeding, examine the child and plot the growth on the chart

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The nurse first establishes what the child can do, what happened around the birth and how the child has grown, and then examines the child before drawing any conclusion

🔍 Key Clues: 18 month old

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — tell the mother to carry the child less often: Advice given before the assessment blames the mother without evidence

B — reassure the mother that all children walk by two years: Reassurance given before an assessment may delay the diagnosis of a developmental problem

C — prescribe calcium supplements alone: Calcium alone treats no cause and no diagnosis has yet been made

⚠️ Exam Trap: In paediatric questions look at the age first - the normal values and the expected action change with age.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse records the milestones month by month rather than in a single line, because a child who is delayed in one area has a very different outlook from a child who is delayed in all of them
option_1: tell the mother to carry the child less often
option_2: reassure the mother that all children walk by two years
option_4: take a full history of the milestones, the birth and the feeding, examine the child and plot the growth on the chart

question: The route that gives the most rapid onset of action in an emergency is:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. intravenous

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The intravenous route puts the whole dose directly into the circulation, so it acts within seconds and gives immediate control over the effect

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — intramuscular: Intramuscular absorption depends on the blood flow to the muscle

C — rectal: Rectal absorption is irregular and slower

D — oral: An oral drug has to be absorbed and acts in half an hour or more

⚠️ Exam Trap: Check the dose, route and timing before choosing - the right drug in the wrong dose is a wrong answer.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse stays with the patient for the first minutes after an intravenous drug, because a reaction to a drug given by vein arrives at the same speed with which the drug was given

question: The prescription reads 1 gram of an antibiotic in 100 mL of normal saline to be given over 30 minutes. The infusion pump should be set at:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. 200 mL per hour

🧠 Clinical Rationale: One hundred millilitres in half an hour is two hundred millilitres an hour, which is the rate to be set on the pump

🔍 Key Clues: 100 mL

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — 100 mL per hour: 100 mL an hour would take a full hour and double the ordered time

C — 400 mL per hour: 400 mL an hour would give the dose in fifteen minutes and risk a reaction

D — 300 mL per hour: 300 mL an hour would finish the bottle in twenty minutes

⚠️ Exam Trap: Check the dose, route and timing before choosing - the right drug in the wrong dose is a wrong answer.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse calculates the hourly rate before priming the line and checks the volume in the burette at the half way point, because a rapid infusion of an antibiotic can drop the blood pressure and give a red man syndrome

question: The normal resting heart rate of a healthy adult is:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. 60 to 100 per minute

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The accepted range for the resting heart rate of a healthy adult is sixty to one hundred beats a minute

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — 40 to 60 per minute: Below sixty is bradycardia in an adult at rest

B — 100 to 120 per minute: Above a hundred is tachycardia

D — 120 to 140 per minute: A rate of 120 to 140 at rest is a marked tachycardia

⚠️ Exam Trap: Know the definition AND the unit - exams love near-sounding concepts.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse compares the pulse with the patient's usual rate and not only with the textbook range, because an athlete whose normal rate is fifty is already tachycardic at ninety

question: The normal adult urinary output in twenty four hours is about:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. 1200 to 1500 mL

🧠 Clinical Rationale: A healthy adult passes about one to one and a half litres of urine in twenty four hours

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — 800 to 1000 mL: This is at the lower edge of normal and below the usual adult output

B — 2500 to 3000 mL: A daily output above about two and a half litres is polyuria

C — 400 to 600 mL: A daily output of less than 400 mL is oliguria

⚠️ Exam Trap: Know the definition AND the unit - exams love near-sounding concepts.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse adds the hourly volumes of the intake output chart rather than estimating the day's total, because an output that is totalled only at midnight is discovered too late to be corrected

question: A patient admitted after a suicide attempt says he still wishes he were dead. The most important nursing action is to:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. ask him directly about his intent, stay with him and remove the means of harm from his reach

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Asking directly about suicidal intent does not plant the idea, and the patient who is at risk is kept under observation with the means of harm removed

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — tell him that such talk is a sin: Moral judgement closes the conversation and increases the isolation

C — change the subject whenever he speaks of death: Avoiding the topic tells the patient that his distress is unwelcome

D — leave him alone so that he can rest: Leaving a suicidal patient alone is unsafe

⚠️ Exam Trap: In mental health questions, choose the response that is non-judgemental and preserves safety first.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse remains with the patient while help is arranged, because the presence of one person who is not shocked is what most often carries a patient through the hour of greatest risk
option_1: ask him directly about his intent, stay with him and remove the means of harm from his reach
option_2: tell him that such talk is a sin
option_3: change the subject whenever he speaks of death
option_4: leave him alone so that he can rest

question: The most reliable method of sterilising a used hypodermic needle is:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. autoclaving at 121 degrees Celsius under 15 pounds pressure for 20 minutes

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Moist heat under pressure at 121 degrees for twenty minutes destroys all micro organisms, including spores and viruses

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — exposure to sunlight: Sunlight has no sterilising power on an instrument

B — soaking in a disinfectant solution: A disinfectant solution destroys many organisms but not all spores

D — washing with soap and water: Washing removes the soil and not the organisms

⚠️ Exam Trap: Separate sterilisation from disinfection, and bacteria from viruses - they are common distractors.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse loads the autoclave loosely and leaves the lids off the drums, because steam that cannot reach the surface of an instrument sterilises the outside of the pack and not the instrument
option_3: autoclaving at 121 degrees Celsius under 15 pounds pressure for 20 minutes

question: The first vascular change at the site of acute inflammation is:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. vasoconstriction followed by vasodilatation

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The vessels narrow briefly at the moment of injury and then dilate, which is why the area is pale for a moment and red soon after

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — clotting of blood in the vessel: Clotting comes later as part of haemostasis

B — immediate and lasting vasodilatation: There is always a short initial constriction

D — constriction of the lymphatics: The lymphatics dilate and carry away the exudate

⚠️ Exam Trap: Distinguish acute from chronic, and reversible from irreversible, before choosing.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse records the warmth and the redness of a wound rather than only its size, because the first two changes are the earliest signs that inflammation is spreading

question: A patient with chronic renal failure on dialysis is usually advised a diet that is:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. low in protein, low in sodium and low in potassium

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Protein, sodium and potassium are all restricted, because the failing kidney cannot excrete their end products and the dialysis can remove only a part of them

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — high in potassium and high in phosphorus: Potassium and phosphorus are retained in renal failure and are restricted

C — low in calories and high in fluid: The fluid is restricted and the calories are kept adequate

D — high in protein and high in sodium: A high protein and high sodium intake overloads a kidney that is already failing

⚠️ Exam Trap: Separate the deficiency disease from its dietary source - exams mix the two.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse teaches the patient to count the potassium in the fruits and the salt in the pickles he eats at home, because the diet sheet is followed only when it is expressed in the food the family actually cooks
option_1: high in potassium and high in phosphorus
option_2: low in protein, low in sodium and low in potassium
option_3: low in calories and high in fluid
option_4: high in protein and high in sodium

question: The Ajanta caves are situated in the state of:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. Maharashtra

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The Ajanta caves with their Buddhist paintings and sculptures lie in the Aurangabad district of Maharashtra

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — Madhya Pradesh: Madhya Pradesh has the Bhimbetka rock shelters

C — Karnataka: Karnataka has the monuments of Hampi and Belur

D — Gujarat: Gujarat has the Rani ki Vav step well and the Modhera sun temple

⚠️ Exam Trap: Beware near-sounding options (Delhi vs New Delhi, Godavari vs Ganga).

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse who knows the historic places of a patient's home state has an opening for conversation, because a long stay patient who is talking about his own district is a patient who is not thinking about his illness

question: The Indian Red Cross Society was founded in the year:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. 1920

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The Indian Red Cross Society was established in 1920 by an Act of the Indian legislature to give relief in sickness, disaster and war

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — 1947: 1947 is the year of independence

C — 1918: 1918 is earlier than its establishment

D — 1930: 1930 is later

⚠️ Exam Trap: Beware near-sounding options (Delhi vs New Delhi, Godavari vs Ganga).

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse who knows the nearest Red Cross branch knows where to send a family for a unit of blood or for relief after a disaster, because in an emergency it is the organisation that can be reached that matters

question: The Chief Justice of India is appointed by:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. the President

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The President appoints the Chief Justice of India and the other judges of the Supreme Court, after consultation where the Constitution requires it

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — the Union Law Minister: The Law Minister is a member of the government and has no such power

B — the Parliament: Parliament makes the law and does not make the appointment

D — the Prime Minister: The Prime Minister heads the government and does not appoint judges

⚠️ Exam Trap: Beware near-sounding options (Delhi vs New Delhi, Godavari vs Ganga).

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse who knows that the law of the land stands above every institution is better able to understand why a patient's right to information is a matter of law and not of a doctor's courtesy

question: The first woman to become the Chief Minister of an Indian state was:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. Sucheta Kripalani

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Sucheta Kripalani became the Chief Minister of Uttar Pradesh in 1963 and was the first woman to hold that office in an Indian state

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — Sarojini Naidu: Sarojini Naidu was the Governor of Uttar Pradesh and never a Chief Minister

C — Vijaya Lakshmi Pandit: Vijaya Lakshmi Pandit was a diplomat and the President of the General Assembly of the United Nations

D — Indira Gandhi: Indira Gandhi became the Prime Minister of India in 1966

⚠️ Exam Trap: Beware near-sounding options (Delhi vs New Delhi, Godavari vs Ganga).

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse who remembers the women who led in public life carries the same expectation into her own profession, because a profession in which women lead a ward also produces the women who lead the institutions

question: The Indira Gandhi Canal lies mainly in the state of:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. Rajasthan

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The Indira Gandhi Canal runs through the Thar desert of Rajasthan and has turned a large tract of barren land into irrigated farmland

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — Gujarat: Gujarat lies to the south of the command area

B — Haryana: Haryana lies to the east of the canal's course

C — Punjab: Punjab is where the canal draws its water

⚠️ Exam Trap: Beware near-sounding options (Delhi vs New Delhi, Godavari vs Ganga).

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse who explains to a village how drinking water and irrigation change the pattern of disease is teaching what the canal itself demonstrates, because water affects health as much as it affects the crop

question: The Battle of Buxar was fought in the year:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. 1764

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The Battle of Buxar was fought in 1764 and its result established the political power of the East India Company in Bengal and Bihar

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — 1767: 1767 falls in the first Anglo Mysore war

C — 1757: 1757 is the year of the Battle of Plassey

D — 1772: 1772 is the year in which Warren Hastings became Governor of Bengal

⚠️ Exam Trap: Beware near-sounding options (Delhi vs New Delhi, Godavari vs Ganga).

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse in an epidemic learns the sequence of events as carefully as a student of history learns a battle, because the first case, the first death and the first report build the chain that the enquiry must follow

question: The body that replaced the Planning Commission of India was set up in the year:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. 2015

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The Planning Commission was replaced by the National Institution for Transforming India, known as NITI Aayog, which was set up in 2015

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — 2014: 2014 is the year of a general election and not the year of the new body

C — 2017: 2017 is later

D — 2012: 2012 is earlier than its setting up

⚠️ Exam Trap: Beware near-sounding options (Delhi vs New Delhi, Godavari vs Ganga).

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse reads the health goals of the country in the policy documents of such bodies, because the immunisation target of the district is drawn from the plan of the nation

question: The National Sports Day of India is celebrated on 29 August in honour of:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. Dhyan Chand

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The National Sports Day marks the birthday of the hockey wizard Dhyan Chand, whose birthday falls on 29 August

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — Kapil Dev: Kapil Dev led India to the cricket world cup in 1983

C — P T Usha: P T Usha is a celebrated athlete and not the person after whom the day is named

D — Milkha Singh: Milkha Singh was a great sprinter and is honoured on other occasions

⚠️ Exam Trap: Beware near-sounding options (Delhi vs New Delhi, Godavari vs Ganga).

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse uses the national days in the ward calendar to plan a health talk, because a day the staff and the patients already remember is the easiest day on which to gather an audience

question: The number of hydrogen atoms in one molecule of water is:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. 2

🧠 Clinical Rationale: A molecule of water has two atoms of hydrogen joined to one atom of oxygen, which is why its formula is written as H2O

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — 1: One atom of hydrogen would give a different compound altogether

B — 4: Four atoms of hydrogen are not present in a molecule of water

C — 3: Three atoms of hydrogen would give oxygen three valencies, which it does not have

⚠️ Exam Trap: Beware near-sounding options and units - define the quantity before choosing.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse knows that a helium cylinder in a ward is kept apart from the oxygen cylinders, because the two look alike and a mix up of an inert gas with oxygen can kill the patient on the trolley

question: The chief function of the platelets in the blood is:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. clotting of blood

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The platelets adhere to the injured vessel wall and release factors that start the chain which forms the clot

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — transport of oxygen: Oxygen is carried by the haemoglobin of the red cells

C — transport of nutrients: Nutrient transport is done by the plasma

D — defence against infection: Defence is the work of the white cells

⚠️ Exam Trap: Beware near-sounding options and units - define the quantity before choosing.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse counts the days after a platelet transfusion for the appearance of new petechiae, because a platelet count that is falling is seen on the skin before it is read on the report

question: The loss of water vapour from the leaves of a plant is called:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. transpiration

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Transpiration is the escape of water vapour through the stomata of the leaves and it pulls the water column up the stem

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — conduction: Conduction is the movement of heat or of a nerve impulse and not of water from a leaf

C — respiration: Respiration is the release of energy from food

D — photosynthesis: Photosynthesis is the making of food in the presence of light

⚠️ Exam Trap: Beware near-sounding options and units - define the quantity before choosing.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse keeps plants out of the immediate breathing zone of an asthmatic patient, because damp soil and dense leaves hold the dust and the spores that provoke the attack

question: The number of bones in the human skull is:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. 22

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The adult skull is made up of twenty two bones, of which eight form the cranium and fourteen the face

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — 14: Fourteen is the number of the bones of the face alone

B — 26: Twenty six is the number of bones in the vertebral column

D — 33: Thirty three is the number of vertebrae in a child before some of them fuse

⚠️ Exam Trap: Beware near-sounding options and units - define the quantity before choosing.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse counts the fontanelles and the sutures of a newborn head at every visit, because a suture that closes early or a fontanelle that is sunken tells of a problem that is easier to treat the earlier it is seen. Clinical point: The nurse who crushes an enteric coated tablet destroys its coating, because a drug that was meant to dissolve in the intestine is released into the acid of the stomach and either burns it or is destroyed itself

question: A deficiency of vitamin K leads to:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. prolonged bleeding

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Vitamin K is needed by the liver for the formation of prothrombin and other clotting factors, so its lack prolongs the bleeding time

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — bleeding gums with swollen joints: Bleeding gums with swollen joints is the picture of scurvy from a lack of vitamin C

B — night blindness: Night blindness is caused by a lack of vitamin A

C — softening of the bones: Softening of the bones follows a lack of vitamin D

⚠️ Exam Trap: Separate the deficiency disease from its dietary source - exams mix the two.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse watches the gum margins, the venepuncture sites and the urine of a patient on a long course of antibiotics, because the gut bacteria that make vitamin K are destroyed by the antibiotic and the bleeding appears without any injury

question: The immunity that a newborn baby receives through the mother's milk is an example of:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. natural passive immunity

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The antibodies in the colostrum are ready made and are passed naturally from the mother to the child, which makes the immunity passive and natural

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — natural active immunity: Active immunity follows an infection or a vaccine and the body makes its own antibodies

C — artificial active immunity: A vaccine is an artificial active immunity

D — artificial passive immunity: An injection of readymade antibodies such as antitetanus serum is an artificial passive immunity

⚠️ Exam Trap: Beware near-sounding options and units - define the quantity before choosing.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse puts the baby to the breast within the first half hour of a normal delivery, because the colostrum that carries those antibodies is produced only in the first days and is never repeated

question: The largest vein of the human body is the:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. inferior vena cava

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The inferior vena cava brings the blood of the lower half of the body back to the right atrium and is the largest vein in the body

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — superior vena cava: The superior vena cava drains the upper half of the body and is smaller than the inferior vena cava

B — hepatic portal vein: The hepatic portal vein is a large vessel of the liver circulation and is smaller still

D — pulmonary vein: The pulmonary veins carry oxygenated blood from the lungs and are smaller

⚠️ Exam Trap: Beware near-sounding options and units - define the quantity before choosing.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse tests the specific gravity of a patient who is passing a large volume of urine, because a low and fixed specific gravity is the earliest sign that the kidney has lost its power to concentrate

question: The vitamin that is largely destroyed by prolonged cooking and over boiling of vegetables is:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. vitamin C

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Vitamin C is water soluble and is destroyed by heat and by long cooking, so vegetables should be cooked briefly in little water

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — vitamin K: Vitamin K is also fat soluble and fairly heat stable

B — vitamin B12: Vitamin B12 is more resistant to ordinary cooking than vitamin C

D — vitamin D: Vitamin D is a fat soluble vitamin and is stable to ordinary cooking

⚠️ Exam Trap: Separate the deficiency disease from its dietary source - exams mix the two.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse teaches the family to cook the vegetables in a covered vessel in the least water and to use that water in the meal, because the vitamin that was dissolved out is thrown away with the water that is poured off

question: In a nursing class of 60 students, 45 passed the examination. The pass percentage is:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. 75 per cent

🧠 Method: Forty five out of sixty is three quarters, and three quarters expressed as a percentage is seventy five per cent

⚡ Fast Approach: Break the percentage into easy parts (10 percent, 5 percent, 1 percent) and add them.

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — 80 per cent: 80 per cent would mean 48 passed

C — 70 per cent: 70 per cent would mean 42 passed

D — 65 per cent: 65 per cent would mean 39 students passed

⚠️ Exam Trap: Do not pick an option only because it is familiar - the option that fits the whole stem is the answer.

💎 PNC Trick: The nurse reduces the fraction before multiplying by a hundred, because a figure that is simplified first is far less likely to be entered wrongly on the report

question: A 500 mL bottle of fluid is to be infused over four hours. The hourly rate is:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. 125 mL

🧠 Method: Five hundred millilitres divided by four hours gives one hundred and twenty five millilitres an hour

⚡ Fast Approach: Write down what is given and what is asked before calculating.

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — 100 mL: 100 mL an hour would take five hours

B — 120 mL: 120 mL an hour would take more than four hours

D — 150 mL: 150 mL an hour would finish the bottle in about three hours twenty minutes

⚠️ Exam Trap: Do not pick an option only because it is familiar - the option that fits the whole stem is the answer.

💎 PNC Trick: The nurse writes the hourly rate on the bottle itself, because the nurse who takes over at the change of shift has the time but not the calculation

question: The average of 5, 9, 13 and 17 is:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. 11

🧠 Method: The four numbers add up to forty four and forty four divided by four gives eleven

⚡ Fast Approach: Total = average x number of items. Find the total first, then subtract the known values.

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — 10: 10 multiplied by four gives 40 and not 44

B — 12: 12 multiplied by four gives 48 and not 44

C — 9: 9 multiplied by four gives 36 and not 44

⚠️ Exam Trap: Do not pick an option only because it is familiar - the option that fits the whole stem is the answer.

💎 PNC Trick: The nurse checks an average by multiplying it back by the number of readings, because a reversed figure is caught at once by that one step

question: An ambulance covers 90 kilometres in one hour and thirty minutes. Its average speed is:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. 60 kilometres an hour

🧠 Method: One hour and thirty minutes is one and a half hours, and ninety divided by one and a half gives sixty kilometres an hour

⚡ Fast Approach: Average speed = total distance / total time - never the mean of the two speeds.

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — 75 kilometres an hour: 75 kilometres an hour would take one hour and twelve minutes

C — 45 kilometres an hour: 45 kilometres an hour would take two hours

D — 50 kilometres an hour: 50 kilometres an hour would take one hour and forty eight minutes

⚠️ Exam Trap: In FIRST-action questions, identify the life-threatening problem and stabilise or assess before anything else.

💎 PNC Trick: The nurse converts the minutes into a fraction of an hour before dividing, because the figure that is not converted is the commonest reason for a transport time that is planned wrong

question: A syrup contains 40 mg of the drug in each millilitre. The volume needed for a 100 mg dose is:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. 2.5 mL

🧠 Method: One hundred divided by forty gives two and a half, so two and a half millilitres contain the hundred milligrams

⚡ Fast Approach: Write down what is given and what is asked before calculating.

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — 4 mL: 4 mL would carry 160 mg

C — 3 mL: 3 mL would carry 120 mg

D — 2 mL: 2 mL would carry only 80 mg

⚠️ Exam Trap: Check the dose, route and timing before choosing - the right drug in the wrong dose is a wrong answer.

💎 PNC Trick: The nurse measures such a small volume in a syringe and never in a spoon, because the difference between two and a half and three millilitres is a quarter of the dose in a child

question: A patient took 2400 mL of fluid in twenty four hours and passed 1800 mL of urine. The approximate insensible loss is:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. 600 mL

🧠 Method: The difference between the intake and the measured output is 600 mL, which is the water lost through the skin, the lungs and the faeces

⚡ Fast Approach: Write down what is given and what is asked before calculating.

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — 400 mL: 400 mL is the loss in a patient who has also been sweating heavily or has had a large stool

B — 500 mL: 500 mL does not balance this chart

D — 700 mL: 700 mL is more than the difference shown by these figures

⚠️ Exam Trap: In FIRST-action questions, identify the life-threatening problem and stabilise or assess before anything else.

💎 PNC Trick: The nurse totals the balance at the same hour every day, because a balance sheet that is added up at a different time each day hides the very trend that it was kept to show

question: Two tablets of a drug contain 500 mg. The number of tablets needed for a dose of 1.5 g is:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. 6

🧠 Method: One and a half grams is 1500 mg, and since 500 mg needs two tablets, 1500 mg needs six

⚡ Fast Approach: Write down what is given and what is asked before calculating.

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — 4: 4 tablets would give 1000 mg

B — 8: 8 tablets would give 2000 mg

D — 5: 5 tablets would give 1250 mg

⚠️ Exam Trap: Check the dose, route and timing before choosing - the right drug in the wrong dose is a wrong answer.

💎 PNC Trick: The nurse converts the grams to milligrams before working out the number of tablets, because a dose that is left in grams and a tablet that is labelled in milligrams is the pair that produces an error of a thousand times

question: Find the odd one out: 2, 4, 6, 9.
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. 9

🧠 Method: Two, four and six are even numbers, while nine is odd

⚡ Fast Approach: Draw the circles of the given sets and see which conclusion is certain.

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — 2: 2 is an even number

B — 4: 4 is an even number

C — 6: 6 is an even number

⚠️ Exam Trap: Look for the qualifier (FIRST / BEST / MOST LIKELY) - it decides the answer.

💎 PNC Trick: The nurse states the shared property in words before choosing, because an odd one out that is chosen by feel is the answer that changes with the mood of the candidate

question: Complete the series: 11, 22, 44, 88, ?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. 176

🧠 Method: Each term is double the term before it, so twice eighty eight gives one hundred and seventy six

⚡ Fast Approach: Check the differences first, then squares, cubes or multiplication.

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — 165: 165 is not double of 88

B — 154: 154 is not double of 88

C — 198: 198 is more than double of 88

⚠️ Exam Trap: Read the stem twice - one word such as MOST or EXCEPT can reverse the answer.

💎 PNC Trick: The nurse checks a doubling series by dividing the last term back, because a series that is doubled by mistake somewhere shows at once when it is halved again

question: If DOG is written as EPH in a certain code, then CAT is written as:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. DBU

🧠 Method: Each letter is moved one place forward in the alphabet, so C becomes D, A becomes B and T becomes U

⚡ Fast Approach: Compare the first and last letters of the given pair to find the shift.

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — EBU: The first letter of CAT is C and not E

C — DCU: The second letter of CAT is A and not C

D — DBV: The last letter of CAT is T and not V

⚠️ Exam Trap: In FIRST-action questions, identify the life-threatening problem and stabilise or assess before anything else.

💎 PNC Trick: The nurse writes the alphabet with the number under each letter before decoding, because a shift that is counted in the head is the step where such questions are usually lost

question: A health worker walks 3 kilometres towards the north and then 4 kilometres towards the east. How far is she from the starting point?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. 5 kilometres

🧠 Method: The two walks are at right angles, so the straight distance is the square root of three squared plus four squared, which is five kilometres

⚡ Fast Approach: Draw a small diagram - each turn changes the direction by a fixed angle.

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — 6 kilometres: 6 kilometres would need sides of about 4.2 and 4.2

C — 7 kilometres: 7 kilometres is the sum of the two walks and not the direct distance

D — 12 kilometres: 12 kilometres is twice their product and has no meaning here

⚠️ Exam Trap: In FIRST-action questions, identify the life-threatening problem and stabilise or assess before anything else.

💎 PNC Trick: The nurse draws the path as a right angled triangle at once, because a patient's home that is five kilometres away as the crow flies may be seven by the road and the visit must be planned on the road distance

question: Pointing to a photograph a man says, she is the daughter of my grandfather's only son. How is the girl in the photograph related to him?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. sister

🧠 Method: The grandfather's only son is the man's own father, and his daughter is the man's sister

⚡ Fast Approach: Draw the family tree and mark the given relations before answering.

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — niece: A niece is the daughter of his own brother or sister

C — aunt: An aunt is a sister of the father or the mother

D — cousin: A cousin would be the daughter of an uncle or an aunt

⚠️ Exam Trap: Do not pick an option only because it is familiar - the option that fits the whole stem is the answer.

💎 PNC Trick: The nurse draws the family as a tree from the oldest person downwards, because a relation that is traced upwards from the speaker is the one that is most often read in the wrong direction

question: Some nurses are teachers. All teachers are graduates. Which of the following follows?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. Some nurses are graduates

🧠 Method: The nurses who are teachers must also be graduates, so at least some nurses are graduates

⚡ Fast Approach: Draw the circles of the given sets and see which conclusion is certain.

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — No nurse is a graduate: It directly contradicts the conclusion that follows

C — All nurses are graduates: Only some of the nurses are teachers and the rest need not be graduates

D — All graduates are nurses: Reversing the second statement does not follow

⚠️ Exam Trap: Do not pick an option only because it is familiar - the option that fits the whole stem is the answer.

💎 PNC Trick: The nurse draws the two circles with the overlap marked before deciding, because a conclusion drawn from the picture cannot be turned round by the reading of a sentence

question: If today is Wednesday, what day of the week will it be after 15 days?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. Thursday

🧠 Method: Fifteen days is two weeks and one day, so the day advances by one from Wednesday and becomes Thursday

⚡ Fast Approach: Use the remainder after dividing by 7 for days, and 30 degrees per hour for clocks.

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — Wednesday: Wednesday would be the day after fourteen days

C — Tuesday: Tuesday is two days before Wednesday

D — Friday: Friday would need sixteen days

⚠️ Exam Trap: Do not pick an option only because it is familiar - the option that fits the whole stem is the answer.

💎 PNC Trick: The nurse divides the number of days by seven and keeps the remainder, because a long leave or a follow up date worked out without that step lands on the wrong day
